## Summary

Did 2.2: `sofar drive` — the stateless loop in packages/engine/src/driver/drive.ts, its CLI skin in cli/drive.ts, and the command wired in cli/index.ts. The loop folds, picks the next task (active-first in the active phase, then plan order, skipping resolved/blocked tasks and phases), launches through the adapter, waits, resolves the session per D3 and appends the handoff; stop rules are closed, max_sessions and cost cap before each launch, needs_user, N consecutive stalls (default 2) and ^C after, and anything thrown becomes run_stopped error — whatever ends a run, a stop lands behind it. Two decisions before the work: D5, handoff reasons read structurally from the fold (needs_user is the named task in `blocked`, task_done needs a write-back AND a resolved task, everything else stalls) rather than matched from write-back prose, with the prompt telling the session to use the blocked lever; D6, one launch directory per RUN instead of a worktree per session (sequential sessions are cumulative, and a fresh checkout loses uncommitted work and node_modules), with a realpath check refusing any --cwd whose log for the initiative is not the log being driven. A multi-session test exposed a real fragility in resolveLaunchedSession: `started` is millisecond-resolution, so a run landing inside one millisecond read every earlier session as ambiguity — it now also takes the session ids folded BEFORE the launch, and the set difference is the exact half. Also: --resume adopts an unstopped run (and its recorded max_sessions) rather than minting a second one over the same work; threshold policy is refused until its nudge hook exists in 2.3. 27 tests in test/drive.test.ts (loop, reasons, stops, preflight, resume, CLI), the fake adapter extended to script a whole RUN, full suite green at 1775. Smoke-tested end to end through the built CLI against a stub claude on PATH: two sessions, two task_done handoffs, cost summed, stop `closed`. SPEC §Driver gained the loop, the reasons and the launch-directory rules; §Acceptance criteria and §CLI gained `sofar drive`; ARCHITECTURE.md gained both modules.
